head.name: @fzlt/core/view-dom
head.lead: A @fzlt/core/actor table drawn as DOM nodes, one per row, pooled. A row's node is made the first time it shows (make(i), default an empty <i>), put in host through the ledger, and kept for good: when the actor dies the node hides (hidden), and when the row lives again (a new actor) the same node comes back. So the page holds at most cap nodes, and engine.destroy() (Recall) takes every one away and leaves the host as it was. Each render it writes, change-only through the ledger: transform (the body's x, y times scale, to 0.01 px, centred on the node unless center: false, turned by the heading a unless turn: false), --hp (hp / max, to 0.01), and data-side / data-kind when a row shows. The look is the page's CSS ([data-side="1"] { … }, width: calc(var(--hp) * 100%)); give hidden the last word if a rule sets display. paint(i, el) runs after for a row's own change-only writes (through engine.ledger). A board that holds still writes nothing and calls no busy(), so an engine with settle sleeps. A death can linger (seconds, with data-dead set, for a CSS fade) and holds the engine awake that long; with reduced motion the node hides at once. The step only counts lingering deaths down: no DOM, no allocation. A moved row costs one transform string in render; a still one costs nothing.
